utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. I see that everyone found its way to Courtroom I, which was available again today. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Is the -- yes, good morning, Ms. Bibles. Any matter to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good mornings, Your Honours. I would like to introduce Mr. Alan Tieger who I don't believe actually needs much introduction but you will be seeing him in this case so I do introduce him in the courtroom to this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I cannot say that his face is totally unfamiliar to this Chamber. Welcome in this courtroom again, Mr. Tieger. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, we are. We are calling Mr. Pereula Spiro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time to raise the following matter. That is associated exhibits with witness Tomislav Savkic. During the testimony of that witness, document D705 was MFI'd, pending an agreement between the parties concerning the original text and translation, and the Chamber wonders whether the parties have agreed on this matter and, if so, what the agreement was. But perhaps you -- yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we're having a meeting with the Prosecution today, and I think that we will then resolve this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll hear from the parties after that meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Pereula. Before you give evidence, the Rules require --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pereula. Please be seated. You will be first examined by Mr. Lukic. You find Mr. Lukic to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pereula, good morning.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, will you please slowly tell us your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: My name is Spiro Pereula, born on the 10th of November, 1941.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens 1D1747, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pereula, did you give a statement to the Mladic Defence team on two occasions?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're now looking at a document signed --

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: On the 17th, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 15th of July, 2014. But I see that -- on the statement, the date of the interview is recorded as being the 5th of March, 2014. Did you speak with General Mladic's Defence at that time?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: No, I did not. From the 5th to the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 5th.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you recognise the signature on the screen, on the page that you are looking at?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature on this page?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who wrote the date at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And is what you told us correctly recorded in this statement?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes. There is one correction, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell us what that is.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: It's on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are not able to hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you are -- could you please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. The letters are very tiny and so I cannot read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please tell us what you're looking for.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Well, what we agreed on, as far as I know, that -- to erase that date when I was in the hospital. That's all. I don't know what page that's on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] I lost it now too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need page 4 and paragraph 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We notified about this, this morning. Mr. Pereula, can you see it?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot find the part that the witness is reading from; interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you were reading from the statement. The interpreters were unable to follow you. Apparently you said something about you being hospitalised and what you agreed that should be taken out. What should be taken out?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just read the part that needs to be deleted.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: "Because I was at the military hospital in Sarajevo for treatment." This is something that needs to be erased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it's not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's true but it wasn't until the 7th. It was until the 3rd. Based on the text, you could conclude that I was in the hospital until the 7th, but actually I was in the hospital until the 3rd of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In Belgrade. And then you returned -- Sarajevo. Yes, yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not in Belgrade. I was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, sorry, that was my mistake. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Other than this correction, it's everything else that was said?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, everything else is accurate and I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to put the same questions to you today, would you give the same answers, in principle?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D1747A, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see the document in front of you, on the right side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: It's mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you see a signature on the last page of the document?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this your statement and is everything recorded accurately, the way you said it?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And is what you said in the statement truthful?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And if you were to be asked the same questions as those, would you give the same answers, in principle?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to tender these two statement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have one question to the witness. When you were asked whether you gave that statement on the 5th of March, you said no, no, no. And then you said the 5th to the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 17th, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that March of this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you signed it -- well, let's say, in July? I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I signed it in July and the interview was also conducted then. Later I got some information that I added, although there isn't that much difference between the first and the second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm a bit confused. You were interviewed in March? During --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And I signed the statement on the 17th -- no, the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear to me, yes. But when you talked about the second statement, what did you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, I didn't understand you. The second statement was a supplemental one because I got some new information. It talks about more details about the torture of Serbs in the Sunce prison in Dobrinja in Sarajevo. And it says in the statement that Serbs were tortured in that prison, my brother was there, and so on and so forth. And the statement was given to the radio television of Republika Srpska, and this is why I did later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that was therefore the day after you had signed the first statement, you were then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, a couple of days -- a couple of days after that. Thank you. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 1D1747 will be Exhibit D779. And 65 ter number 1D1747A will be Exhibit D780, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D779 and D780 are admitted into evidence. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would just briefly discuss the only associated exhibit. And I spoke with Mr. Weber this morning. We want to make clear on the record that with this associated exhibit, which is video with the transcript, we will rely only on the words uttered by the Mr. Midhat Brica, not on the words uttered by presenters, male or female presenter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With that understanding, the Prosecution has no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you want to tender it as an associated exhibit now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would tender it, then I would not have any questions for this witness. I would just read his statement summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's fine. Although usually with recordings and videos, the Chamber would -- might like -- might want to have a look at it as well so as to see whether there are any further questions. Are you dealing with it Mr. Weber in any --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then if Mr. Weber is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- dealing with it, I can play it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How long is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It has to be played twice probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, is there a transcript? Because the Chamber -- whether we really want to look at it may also depend on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is a transcript. We can see it on our screens. It's 1D03030.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll read the transcript during the first break and see whether it's of any use to watch the video at all or whether we are fully informed by having read the transcript. Yes. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you have any further questions. If you want to read the summary, then you have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. As a professional soldier, Mr. Pereula performed duties at the Territorial Defence Staff of BiH since 1977. The war found him on the position of assistant to the chief of security organ at the Territorial Defence Staff of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He witnessed the escalation of ethnic tensions as early as after the first multi-party elections. Fearing that the weapons and equipment might come in the hands of extremists from all three peoples, the commander of the Republic Territorial Defence Staff then ordered increased measures of securing the warehouses, while part of the materiel was moved to the JNA storages. He is familiar with the fact that the then-Colonel Jovan Divjak, who later became a general of the Muslim forces, issued weapons to the B and H MUP and to the Kiseljak and Kresevo Territorial Defence without knowledge and approval of the commander of the Republic Territorial Defence Staff. He will describe how the then-Colonel Hasan Efendic took over the duty of commander of the Territorial Defence Staff of B and H on 7 April 1992 and completely divided the staff by ethnic lines. Mr. Pereula then moved to the 2nd Military District Command, and on 19th April he went to Pale and took part in the establishing of the Serb Territorial Defence, while the Muslims had already established their Army of the Republic of B and H. When the VRS was established, he came to the Main Staff of the VRS as a clerk at the sector for intelligence and security affairs, and in late 1993 he was moved to the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska. He remained on that position throughout the war. He will testify about General Mladic as a person and as a soldier. Also, he will describe the way of communication with the VRS Main Staff by way of dispatches. Because he lived in Sarajevo with his family before the war, Mr. Pereula will present his observations about the situation in Sarajevo following the multi-party elections. He will testify about kidnapping and monstrous torching of his brother by the Muslims at the camp for Serbs located in the basement of the Sunce cafe at Dobrinja. That was short statement summary and we do not have questions for this witness at this moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Pereula, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Weber. I'll find Mr. Weber to your right. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Lukic has read a summary of your statement and has no further questions, but that means that the Judges have read your statement so they are aware of what your evidence is up till this moment. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Pereula.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, today I'd like to start off by discussing the securing of weapons before the war. This something you discuss in paragraphs 5 and 6 of your 15 July 2014 statement. In paragraph 5 of your statement, you state: "After the multi-party elections of 1990, and especially during 1991, the interethnic tensions increased at the TO Staff as well." For clarity, when you refer to the multi-party elections, is it correct that you are talking about the multi-party elections held on 18 November 1990?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the multi-party elections. I'm talking about the consequences of the multi-party elections as they reflected on members of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please come closer to the microphone when speaking. Could the usher assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, we'll come to that in a second. But I just want to know when you are referring to the multi-party elections, you were referring to the elections held on 18 November 1990; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P3083.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, sir, I understand that it's your evidence that your view is that as a consequence of these elections, there was certain actions taken to secure the weaponry. I'd like to look at some documentation and then I'll come back to that. This is a 14 May 1990 SSNO order numbered 19-1 from Blagoje Adzic concerning the safekeeping -- sir can you see it? It's related to the safekeeping of weapons and ammunition of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, maybe to assist the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- if we could just get the B/C/S enlarged for the witness on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And could the usher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could the usher assist on a constant basis that the microphone is always situated in such a way. And could we have enlarged this portion because it's not easy to read it. Any specific part, Mr. Weber, you want to?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was just coming to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to item 1, General Adzic orders the various military commands together with the TO Staffs of the republics and provinces to "take other storage and safekeeping of the complete stock of the TO weapons and ammunition in the JNA supply dumps and depots." Sir, before I ask my question, do you see that portion?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you aware of this order?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I did not know about it. This something that only senior-ranking officers could have known about, such as the commander of the Republican Staff of the TO, and then he was the one who would proceed to issue specific orders to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that TO weapons and ammunition were relocated to JNA facilities before 14 June 1990?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I could not say anything specific, no. I mean, this was written up -- well, what I should say first is that the ammunition and weapons of the Territorial Defence were partly in our depots that were not of the JNA, and then part of them were in JNA depots. After this escalation, a conclusion was reached; namely, that our warehouses were not safe. And an order was issued: Wherever there are JNA depots nearby and of the Territorial Defence, the weapons should be transferred there. For example, in Kiseljak, There was a JNA depot and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, we have your statement. There is no need to repeat it. I appreciate what your statement says. My question was were you aware specifically about the relocation of TO weaponries into JNA facilities. I'll broaden it a little bit more. Were you aware of any relocation prior to the multi-party elections in November 1990?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 02960 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that, maybe it's important to record on the transcript that date of this order is the 14th of May, 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Pereula, this is a 13 September 1990 Socialist Republic of BiH Republican Territorial Defence Staff report from commander Milos Bajcetic. It's related to the better protection of the armaments and ammunition of the TO of the SRBiH. I'd like to direct your attention before I ask some questions to the first part. At the beginning of the report, Commander Bajcetic refers to the 14 May 1990 order number 19-1 from Blagoje Adzic, which we just saw. In the second paragraph, the report states: "The relocation of the TO SRBiH armaments and ammunition was carried out between 18 May and 23 May 1990 with the exception of the region of Bihac and Banja Luka where it was completed on 13 June 1990." Do you see these portions of the report?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, based on this information, it appears that there was quite significant steps taken to relocate the weapons. As an official in the Security Administration, how is it that you were not aware of this?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. Because links with the commander of the Territorial Defence -- or rather, it was my commander, Nikola Andjelic, who was the person through who I communicated or they were the ones who communicated with the main command. And then at that meeting these questions were resolved. At the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina, we had District Staffs of the Territorial Defence and there was a security organ in every District Staff, and I was not involved directly to go there and do that. That was done by the security organs in that area and other organs who were needed in order to have this carried out. I just knew that weapons and ammunition needed to be placed there where they would have proper security. In these concrete cases it was not my task and I didn't do that, and it's possible I didn't -- well, when the situation got worse - that's 1991 - and when Yugoslavia was broken up and so on, then I was more involved in the protection of facilities in the area of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, this is a very long answer, but I understand the issue to be that in your statement, you say that it happened after the multi-party elections, whereas the document shown to you suggests that it happened well before that date. So apart from your explanations --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm saying, I am telling you about when I found about this problem about this case. I'm speaking about myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, in your statement you are telling us what happened. You do not say, I learned about this at that point in time. No. You say this happened after the multi-party elections, whereas the document suggests, and it seems that you do not disagree necessarily with that, that it happened well before the multi-party elections. That's the issue apparently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm not denying that. But what I am saying is when I found out about this, and this document shows that this happened in 1990, that the order arrived. But I mean, at that time I did not know about that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all fine and we now understand it, but that's not what your statement sayings. Your statement doesn't say I learned about this at that point in time. The statement says it happened then. And that is therefore, if I understand you well, unreliable because it's -- relates to the time you learned about it which is different from the time when it happened. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 2960 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P6911, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Pereula, I want to go forward to the spring of 1992. In paragraph 9 of your 15 July 2014 statement, you state: "At the end of March and the beginning of April, the whole city was under barricades." Is it correct that the JNA 2nd Military District had been distributing weapons to Territorial Defence Staffs in the area of Sarajevo prior to the end of March 1992?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to look at something then specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 18369 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a 2 March 1992 order from Colonel General Kukanjac of the 2nd Military District. According to this document, Kukanjac instructs subordinate commands to issue 250 7.62-millimetre automatic rifles to the Novo Sarajevo TO Staff. How is it that you were not aware of this in your position as a member of the Territorial Defence Staff of the republican TO?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Well, I did not belong to the command of the 2nd Military District. That did not go through the Republican Staff or Territorial Defence. The Territorial Defence was most certainly not aware of that. It went down the chain to the subordinated commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm a bit at loss for a portion of your answer there, since it appears that these weapons are directed to the Territorial Defence Staff in Novo Sarajevo. Do you have anything to say about that?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I have nothing to say. I don't know about any of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender 65 ter 18369 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6912, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P4932 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to now return to the security of weaponry in JNA facilities. This is a 7 March 1992 2nd Military District order from General Kukanjac. Under item 1, he orders all levels of commands to reassess the level of risk to facilities, personnel, and MTS and take measures that will guarantee their full security. Do you see this portion?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I see the document, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd also like to focus your attention under item 10 where General Kukanjac orders materiel, particularly weapons, ammunition, and MES, which cannot be defended successfully to be transferred to appropriate locations in good time. Are you aware of any actions undertaken by the Territorial Defence in relation to this order?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: You mean this paragraph 10?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, do we see only part of paragraph 10 in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. When in my statement I spoke about things, it is precisely these things that I meant. That is to say, I've already said this, there were Territorial Defence depots that were not safe for ammunition and weapons and then this was transferred to JNA depots, and I meant the period when I was familiar with all of this. I mean during that first period when you took me to 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, to answer your question, no, all paragraph 10 is not currently on the screen in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have the part you quoted on our screens. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I actually have no further questions on the document. I don't know if Your Honours have any more now seeing the full text. I'm sorry for that inconvenience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I have no further questions at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going move on to a different topic and discuss, actually, your activities during the war. Is it correct that you dealt with the exchange of prisoners from the KPD Butmir, that facility?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you -- took part actually in meetings at the Sarajevo airport regarding the exchange of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that representative -- or at least a representative of the ICRC attended these meetings?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I cannot remember. As a rule he should have been there, but I cannot remember now. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Maybe this will refresh your recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 06175.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a report on a meeting held at the Sarajevo airport on Wednesday, the 6th of October, 1993. It deals with the release -- I'm going to read it to you.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't have any translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to read it to you. Let me know if you have any questions. It deals with the release of detainees from Tarcin and Kula. Did you -- were you aware of the Kula prison?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this document in attendance were a number of individuals, including a representative of UNPROFOR, the ICRC, an UNMO representatives of the BiH, and three representatives from the Bosnian Serb army, the VRS, including Colonel Magazin, Colonel Beara, and yourself. According to these -- according to this report there's a discussion of an exchange of prisons between the Kula and Tarcin facilities. Do you recall this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: No, really I cannot remember this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall having meetings like this where you would discuss the exchange of prisoners in the presence of Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: No. This was the first time I was with Colonel Beara and I never attended an exchange with him after that. I was a member of the commission on behalf of the Army of Republika Srpska, this commission for the exchange of information, and in that capacity I attended meetings down there at the airport. But when I was present, no one was ever exchanged because this was done in different ways, along different lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, you said you don't remember this meeting, but in the same breath you say this is only time that you were in a meeting with Colonel Beara. How do you remember that you were in this meeting with Colonel Beara if you can't remember this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot deny what is written here. I don't remember this meeting, that I was there with Beara. But that's what's written here and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me stop you. Let me stop you, sir. You didn't say you don't deny, you say you don't remember. I'm not asking you about any denial. You say you don't remember the meeting, but you know that this is a meeting -- the only meeting that you had with Colonel Beara. I'm just asking how do you remember that if you don't remember, the meeting itself? I'm not talking about denials.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all right. I came to the conclusion that this was a meeting with Beara because I saw this on this list and maybe it was a slip of the tongue. Maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. The fact that Colonel Beara is mentioned reminds you now of this meeting. You do remember this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I make clear to you that you should not draw conclusions on the basis of what you see on your screen. You should tell us what your recollection is. So don't say that was the only meeting I had with Beara if you have no recollection whatsoever about having been in a meeting with Beara. You're not supposed to interpret what you see on the screen. You're supposed to tell us what you remember that happened at the time. And if you've forgotten about it, there's no problem. But we'd rather know then. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would tender this document but we ask to have it MFI'd for the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI'd P6913.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Pereula, is it correct that civilians were kept in the Kula prison?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I don't know about that because I was not present down there. Other persons worked down there in security. I never visited Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31595.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we look at that, could I seek clarification of one of the previous answers of the witness. You said you were a member of the commission on behalf of the Army of Republika Srpska, the commission for the exchange of information. Was that about prisoners or was it not about prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was a member of the Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners of War on behalf of the Army of Republika Srpska. And there were other members of the commission on behalf of the government, so I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, please limit your answers to my questions. When you had these meetings at the airport, with whom did you have those meetings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had meetings with the other side, with the representatives of the Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And you said no prisoners were exchanged there; I understand that. But the subject of discussion was the exchange of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you had no knowledge where these prisoners came from or where they were detained, or did you have any knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not. We had the task to exchange people, but since we could not reach a concrete agreement, I don't know of concrete cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, may I put a follow-up question. Just now you said, "We had the task to exchange people..." What kind of people are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically my task was to exchange military persons, military personnel, and other members of the commission probably had the task to exchange other people who had been taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What kind of other people? Are you talking about civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I mean prisoners of war, civilians and soldiers and officers who had been taken prisoner, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know it's a little bit early but I just have -- before going into -- I don't have much more, so before going into a whole subject and then returning to it after the recess, is there any way we can just take the quick break and then I will finish rather quickly in the next session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the estimate was two and a half hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe it is one and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One and a half. So you'll be considerably shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll be within -- based on the answers of the witness, yes, I'll finish well within the hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let's first -- Witness, we'll take a break of 20 minutes and we'd like to see you back after that break. And I'm looking at you, Mr. Lukic, the next witness is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next witness is coming in the next week. You know that we have shortcoming this week since one of our witnesses got sick. And we -- [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. But did you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We didn't bring anybody. We couldn't bring anybody else. And we didn't expect to finish this early today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because I remember earlier I asked you whether the next witness would be available and you told us that he was and that's true, but that's -- the follow-up was not available is -- I think it would be have been wiser if you would have warned us that we would have known already in advance that there was a fair chance that would you run out of witnesses this week. Let's take the break first and let's resume -- well, let me be generous again. 22 minutes. Ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, I'd also briefly like to deal with 65 ter 1D02733 which was tendered during the testimony of Mane Djuric. The decision on the admission of this 40-page document was deferred, pending an agreement between the parties concerning the ethnicity of people listed in the document and about the number of pages which should be received in evidence. On the 11th of November the Prosecution informed the Chamber that it had not reached an agreement with the Defence concerning the ethnicity of people listed in the document. On the same day the Defence requested the admission into evidence of the entire 40-page document, and the Chamber would like to hear the position of the Prosecution concerning the admission of the whole of the document but not necessarily immediately because we're not -- we'd prefer that we first focus on hearing the evidence of Mr. Pereula.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just one housekeeping matter related to this witness. The Prosecution has received the B/C/S translation for 65 ter 06175, which was just marked for identification this morning as P06913. We just wanted to inform the Chamber that the translation is now uploaded under document ID ZA018615BCS -- BC. Excuse me. The Prosecution would just ask that the Court Officer be instructed to attach the translation and the document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The instruction is given accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection against admission? Not. Then P6913, once the translation is attached, is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Pereula, before the break, we were discussing the commission that you were a part of. The president of that commission was Captain Dragan Bulajic; correct?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 31595.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a Republika Srpska government central commission for the exchange of prisoners and civilians list containing information on persons from KPD Butmir. Just so you know, this document was recovered from the Office of the Prosecutor from KPD Butmir. You are mentioned throughout this report, and I just want to go through some of the information with you today, if you could assist us. The first person listed is a Mr. Ahmic. According to the description --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And maybe if we could increase the -- the top portion of the B/C/S version for the witness on the page before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The first person listed is a Mr. Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Something is crossed out in my version. I don't have that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whatever is crossed out, you don't have to worry about that. Just follow carefully what Mr. Weber brings to your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The first person is Mr. Ahmic. According to this description Mr. Ahmic was a Muslim who is transferred to another prison on 13 December 1992, and he was on a list of persons from Manjaca that was held in KPD Dom Butmir. Did you have access to this type of information as part of your involvement with the exchange commissions?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I am not aware of this, no. I wasn't engaged on the transfer of persons from the Kula prison to ... to other prisons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You are mentioned in this description as providing information on 24 April 1993. Is it correct that you provided information on detainees that were being kept in various detention facilities?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat whether he said yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, Witness. I think you said no. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Meaning that you did not provide that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, where can we see the witness's name on this part of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, according this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- document, it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Oh yes, I see it now on the seventh line. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you. Occupation, driver; ethnicity, Muslim -- I'm sorry. This is the wrong description. Occupation, tile layer; nationality, Muslim; currently held in Lukavica prison according to information received from Major Pereula in Crna Rijeka on 24 April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see that reference?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I can see that. I can see that, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat what you said after: I see that. What did you then say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I did not provide this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, it's not our position that you provided all of this information, but is it correct that you did provide information? Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I did not provide information at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You do agree that this is a reference to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: That's what it's -- says, but I did not do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Further along in this description, it indicates that Soniboj Skrljevic provided information that Mr. Ahmic was killed by a sniper on 13 April 1994. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes. In 1993, 1994, yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that as part of your role in the exchange commission you became aware of prisoners who were dying in detention facilities, like Mr. Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that either. If I can explain my reply -- or my role in the commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you first explain why such information, as you say, is not accurate, is not true, would appear in this document? If you have any explanation for it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have a specific explanation. I don't know how this came about, but -- I don't know. For sure, I did not ever provide information of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, my question wasn't -- my last question wasn't necessarily meant to intend that you provided such information. But is it correct you received such information?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I did not receive such information either. This is why I wanted to explain my role as a member of this commission. I did not receive this kind of information, and I did not send out this kind of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to go through a couple of more examples and maybe we can figure this out together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could explain what his role was where he apparently was not privy to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- information, either receiving or providing. Could you explain what your role was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners of War was formed under the government of Republika Srpska, and this lasted for a while, for a considerable period of time, and then the government also said that there should be a representative of the Army of Republika Srpska there. So then after two or three months, once the commission existed, I was assigned by the Main Staff to be a member of this commission, and so I attended the sessions of the commission with Captain Bulatovic [as interpreted], who was the president, and there were two or three other members, and Amir Masovic was in the commission as a representative of the Muslim side. When I would come to these meetings, for the most part we would discuss in general how prisoners of war should be exchanged. And while I was in the commission, we did not -- we did not actually exchange a single prisoner of war. When I saw that, I orally informed the Main Staff that there's no role for me in this commission because real things are not being discussed in the commission when I am present. So I attended the commission sessions very rarely. Nothing would ever be resolved. But I was never officially removed as a member of the commission, even though I wasn't a member of it anymore. So I was there in the initial period, and all this information and data was not conveyed through me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But if I may just ask a question, sir. We understand your explanation. But this document on the screen here describes a meeting at which you were present, your name is being mentioned in this particular document. So is it possible that this could be one of the few meetings that you attended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was on the 8th of September, 1993. I don't recall this meeting. I don't recall that we ever exchanged a single prisoner of war while I was a member of the commission, and I personally never sent out any information about prisoners of war to any of the prisons, and I never received such information, in turn, from the prisons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to clarify some things that just -- on the transcript. In your last answer, in your last longer answer, the transcript records you as saying the president of the commission was Captain Bulatovic. Is it correct that you mean to be referring to Dragan Bulajic?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: No. Dragan Bulajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, that's clear. You said you were appointed to the commission by the VRS Main Staff. Who appointed you?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I cannot remember now. I received an order. Probably it was the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 31595 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6914, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30761 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, just glancing through the document we just looked at, I saw that it was not only in relation to the first witness -- to the first person, but that for -- I went now to three, but that in all of those reports it is said that Mr. Pereula provided information.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's most, not all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- but, yes, there are the -- [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- ones I saw, the first three.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, are you aware that for some of the other persons which were discussed in this document that you're also referred to as a person who provided information although on some, I do understand also, you were not mentioned as someone who provided information? Any explanation for this not happening once but a number of times in this document? And sometimes not being mentioned, which means that it was apparently not an automatism. Yes. No, I'm still talking about the previous document, Witness, so don't -- you don't have to read what's on your screen now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was officially appointed to be a commission member by the Main Staff, and those who were in the main commission knew it as well as the others knew it. However, I'm saying now that my role in that was a minor one. I simply had the feeling that I was not accepted in the commission, and it's possible that in view of the fact that this was a -- an official thing, whoever drafted the document, they put me into the document in the belief that I was an official representative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And sometimes they do mention you and sometimes they apparently do not mention you, so it's apparently not something of an automatic nature, but it's -- it's -- seems to be more than that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I am asserting is this: When we're talking about specific persons, I was never present and I never provided any information about specific persons. Meaning, in meetings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But also not outside meetings. You said you never provided any information. Your role was minimal? Or did you ever provide information? On whatever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never gave any information to the prisons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What -- to the commission. Did you provide any information about whatever matter directly related to your position in the commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I never did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Before you, this is a 24 April 1993 VRS Main Staff urgent request from General Manojlo Milovanovic. In the first part of this request, it states: "With the aim of providing details of prisoners to the GS VRS," the Main Staff, "and conducting talks on the exchange of prisoners of war and civilians, compile or update and send us the following lists ..." Do you see this part? It's at the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: List of prisoners of war, a list of all those detained in the territory, all who are in the village of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you don't have to read the document to me.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Could you -- could you please read that once again. I wasn't following.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I am starting at the very beginning, the part that says: "With the aim" -- that starts: "With the aim of..." and then goes on to say -- sir --

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Providing details. That what's it says here. Providing details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, Witness. Mr. Weber, would you please read to the witness what you consider relevant. And, Witness, would you not further look at your screen but carefully listen to what Mr. Weber reads.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to focus your attention on the first part which states: "With the aim of providing details of prisoners to the GS VRS and conducting talks on the exchange of prisoners of war and civilians, compile or update and send us the following lists ..." Do you see that beginning portion?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I wasn't following him now. I need to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you hear -- Mr. Weber read to you how it starts. Mr. Weber, could you please put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Main Staff would send orders to compile or update lists of prisoners to all subordinate VRS corps, as we see here?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. Perhaps the Main Staff did that along a different line from a higher level. I wasn't in the situation to know that. The principle of subordination is such that when information is given, it's issued only to those authorised to receive or know that information. I am not aware of this. I didn't need to know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's focus on another part of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could go towards the bottom of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, sir, it's towards the bottom in front of you too. In the last paragraph, General Milovanovic states: "Upon completion of this task, immediately begin compiling or updating lists of Serbian prisoners of war, civilian prisoners and detainees in prisons in Muslim-controlled territory, as well as prisoners of war in prisons in Muslim-controlled territory..."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please have the next page of the English:

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "... and Muslim prisoners of war and captured civilians in the prisons of the RS." That last part about the Muslim prisoners of war and captured civilians in the prisons of the RS, that is a reference to civilians in the prisons of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Prisons in Republika Srpska and prisons in the Muslim part as well. They're asking for Muslims, civilians, and captured Muslim civilians in the prisons of Republika Srpska, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And this is the type of information you had available to you, right, in your role in the exchange commission?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I am saying again all such orders and requests were sent by the staff command, higher-ranking organs such as the chief here, Manojlo Milovanovic, and all of that was sent to lower commands, corps. The corps were obliged to provide this information, again, on the basis of information from their subordinate units, brigades. So none of that was conveyed through me. All of that went by other channels, not through me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, could I -- Witness, this document clearly states that it aims at obtaining information about persons detained in view of discussions for exchange. Now whether you saw this document or not, were you aware that such information was gathered for the discussions on the exchange?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you never received or obtained information which one would expect to be gathered on the basis of such a -- such an order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was not the system of our work. That means that I was outside of all of that, although I had been appointed. But I did not receive this information, I did not gather this information, and this information did not go through me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As you explained before, you had no idea what happened there. Did you ever ask for your resignation in writing? Because you were not informed, you did not play any role, you were there just for nothing. That's at least how I understand your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you never -- and you never asked for your resignation in writing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never asked for that in writing, but orally, yes. And I was discharged from that duty only after the war ended. And it was done officially by the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are aware that if the Chamber receives this type of evidence, written evidence, documentary evidence, that it might assist us in interpreting it if someone would explain to us what it was all about. But do I understand you well that you are not in a position in any way to further explain what we see here, apart from that you didn't know about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not in a position to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll have to do -- we'll have to interpret this evidence without being assisted by your knowledge. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to give you a fair opportunity to comment consistent with my own obligations here before the Chamber. We saw a document where you were -- according to it where you were providing information to the exchange commission. The date of that information even that we specifically looked at was 24th of April, 1993. And incidentally here we now look at another document dated the same day where this information is being collected by the Main Staff. I see that you're smiling and that you smiled at a response to a couple of my answers. I put it to you that based on your role in the commission that your evidence is actually not accurate. Do you have any other comment?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could the Prosecution -- or the Prosecution tenders this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6915, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 06178 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this next document is, I believe, a document that you saw before in the Popovic case. This is a 13 June 1993 request from you. Is it correct that you sent this document from the Drina Corps IKM in Cajnice?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you sent it from the Drina Corps forward command post in Cajnice; correct?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We see the stamp from the command of the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, indicating this was received on the same date. Is it correct that you sent this document to Colonel Miletic in the Security Administration of the 1st Podrinje Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You state at the beginning of the document: "Muslim armed forces in Gorazde have been placed in a very unfavourable position. Soldiers and citizens are in a state of panic." Is it correct that this was the outcome of VRS operations and activities in the area of Gorazde prior to this date, before the 13th of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Sorry, what was that question? Could you please repeat that question. I really do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And could you speak, please, into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No problem, sir.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I would just like to ask him to repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course. I'm going --

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: What's the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No problem. You state at the beginning of the document: "Muslim armed forces in Gorazde have been placed in a very unfavourable position. Soldiers and citizens are in a state of panic." Is it correct that this was the outcome of VRS operations in the area of Gorazde prior to June -- 13 June 1993?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Well, at any rate, these were the consequences of that combat. I cannot remember the dates when all of this happened; but, at any rate, this happened before my report. I mean, the consequences of combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the next sentence, you state: "We decided to use propaganda more in order to carry out further combat activities and realise our goal (liberation of Gorazde) as successfully as possible." When you say "we decided," you were referring to the -- to a decision of the VRS Main Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: No, no. I would have to explain this a bit. First of all, we were not liberating Gorazde. Before that, in August 1992, we were --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: -- we had left and our task was to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: -- return this territory and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, my question is much more focused about that. There is a specific reference that you are writing here that you say "we decided to use more propaganda." Who is the "we" that decided to use more propaganda, who are you referring to, the "we"?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: The forward command post, the command of the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Then when you state "our goal (liberation of Gorazde)," you're referring to a goal of the VRS then; correct?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to our units, our command, that received that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not sure, just based on what happened, that that was the complete answer. Was that your complete answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I would like to ask you. You said of the orders you received, could you tell us from whom you received those orders for the liberation of Gorazde? The task, I should say, not orders. But who gave you that task?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Main Staff gave us that task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But we were not liberating Gorazde. We were returning lost territories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's all fine, but the document which you sent says "liberation of Gorazde." But you are now interpreting that, which is fine, and we have then the text and your interpretation. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to the next paragraphs, a message was composed which was intended to be broadcast on air on radios in Foca, Visegrad, and Rudo as well as on a megaphone from a moving armoured combat vehicle. You then provide the text of the message, and it starts: "Muslims from Gorazde ..." Is it correct that this message was directed to all Muslims in Gorazde and not just soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: No, just soldiers and officers. And this message did not even reach the soldiers or officers or citizens of Gorazde because, to this day, that population lives in Gorazde and even then they did not react to this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please not lean back all the time but rather come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that the answer you just gave is somewhat inconsistent from a previous answer you gave during the Popovic proceedings, where you were asked at transcript page 24194: "Now, that is a message, I suggest to you, first of all, wait for the question, first of all, it's directed to the Muslims of Gorazde, isn't it? That doesn't say soldiers?" Your answer was: "Yes." Do you have any comment?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I do. I think this is an error made by the person who was typing. And it was in war time. But I as the drafter never meant that. I meant officers and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me interrupt you right away. Do you think that your answer in the Popovic case was wrongly recorded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll verify that on the basis of the audio, Witness, because we -- we very much are in favour of accuracy in this respect. Mr. Weber, I take it that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- proper care will be taken, that you verify, and if there is any -- it would be only fair to the witness that if there is a mistake then, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yeah. It is, Your Honours -- we've discussed or our position is that the official transcript does accurately record it and of course we'll check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Would you please do that and then inform the Defence about the outcome of your check as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The body of the message states: "You have realised that both of world and Alija have left you high and dry. Allah himself will help you if you listen to us. We offer you salvation because we are the only ones who can save you. Break up from those who have driven to you death for months and take the road to salvation. Head towards Kopaci and Ustipraca. There we guarantee you life and final relief. There we offer you shelter and deliverance, and then a road of your choice. It is far away from the hell Alija took you to. Hoist the white flag and be on your way. We are waiting for you in Ustipraca. You don't have much time." Isn't it correct that you intended in this message to have the Muslims in Gorazde surrender and leave?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: No. In war time, of course all propaganda is allowed. Well, not all propaganda, but propaganda that ensures victory. So through this propaganda, I did not mean all citizens. I was referring to soldiers and officers. We were not fighting with civilians, with citizens. We were fighting soldiers and officers, and all of this, what I said, has to do with officers and soldiers in order to create a feeling of uncertainty among them and in order to win the battle. It did not pertain to civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Nowhere in this message do you differentiate between civilians and soldiers; correct?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I agree that that is not written here, but I repeat: The typist, who was not knowledgeable at all -- I mean, this is not even military terminology. Oh, all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Excuse me, did you sign this document, sir, before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you saw that it says "Muslims from Gorazde." It doesn't say "soldiers."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, at that moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- when war operations are under way and -- oh, all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you signed it saying "Muslim," not "soldiers." Just answer my question. You did sign it notwithstanding that it says "Muslims." You know that. The typist doesn't know. You know better.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know. I didn't know what he knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No. You've just told us that this is not military terminology, the typist didn't know, but you didn't mean Muslims you meant soldiers, and I'm saying you signed this document referring to Muslims, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, we are spending already quite a lot of time on it. Do you need any further details?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, I think the meaning of it and the witness's answers, the Chamber is able to assess it. The Prosecution would tender 65 ter 06178 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6916 [Realtime error read in transcript "6196"].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, are you seeking a clarification of the -- ah, I see you have it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was an incomplete exhibit number on the record which is now corrected. And when you said the Prosecution has no, may I understand it that it -- you have no further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, any questions in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just shortly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens P3083.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pereula, which organ issued this document?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: The organ? SSNO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell us what that means, SSNO?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Federal National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Federal Secretariat?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Federal Secretariat for National Defence of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With its seat in?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. In your paragraph, you speak of -- that's paragraph 5 of your statement, the one of the 5th of March, which is D779. You speak of the commander of the RS TO BiH.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does this mean?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: The Republic Staff of Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that paragraph you say that after the multi-party elections in 1990, especially in 1991, interethnic tensions went up in the TO Staff and the commander of the staff of the TO as a result of the fear and the estimation that the weapons would come into the hands of extremists of any nation, in order to prevent this the commander of the Territorial Defence Staff issued an order to increase the security?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let us look at document --

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: This -- this here, well, now, who was this sent to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you want us to stay with this document?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes. This was not sent to the Republic Staff of Territorial Defence. It was sent to subordinated units and the republic staff never received this order from 1990. And I said that in my statement, and then this is being invoked. And look at this: The 1st Army, 2nd, 3rd, and at the end you see this. So this does not pertain to the Republic Staff of Territorial Defence and that is what I referred to in my statement and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, could you please speak more slowly so that the interpreters can follow you. But I think they just managed until now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you don't have to repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let us take a look at the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we asked for document P6911.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do that, Mr. Lukic. Is it true, Witness, that where you suggested that the federal level was separate from the republican level, that in paragraph 1 it reads the Military District, air force, and naval district commands together with the TO Staffs of the socialist republics which links at least this initiative to the TO Staff at the republican level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
