utterances.text: [Interpretation] The order of subordinate units, and that includes the staff of the Territorial Defence, will be a different order based on this order and that will happen later because in Bosnia-Herzegovina this escalation started later as compared to other republics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said the republic staff, talking about the TO Staff, never received this order. How do you know? Where it's addressed to the Republican Staffs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. No. I do apologise if I said it never arrived. I don't know whether they did receive it, or when. Probably now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. If you don't know, then Mr. Lukic may have more questions for you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] So could please have P6911 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document does show, after all, that the Republican Staff of Territorial Defence acted on the basis of the preceding document. That can be seen from paragraph 1. However, it was put to you that on that occasion this operation had been completed, or rather that what is in paragraph 2 -- well, it's written here the relocation of the weapons and ammunition of the TO SRBiH was carried out from the 18th of May until the 23rd of May 1990 with the exception of the region of Bihac and Banja Luka where it was completed on the 13th June 1990. This is what I'm going to ask you now. I'm going to ask you about the paragraphs that follow and that read as follows. Two paragraphs below this one, this is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the last paragraph on this page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "The action applied to the armaments and ammunition of the Territorial Defence and to other actors, only if so desired and explicitly requested. The action did not cover the armaments and ammunition of TO war units formed by work organisations." In 1991, did you actually deal with this as well, inter alia; that is to say, TO units that were formed by work organisations and their weaponry?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes. All this fell under the Republican Staff of the TO and that was only natural, and then the weapons were not properly secured there so it was only natural that it had to be transferred so that proper security could be provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in view of the previous answer of the witness that he doesn't know whether these orders were received, et cetera, we should always lay a foundation because the witness now tells us what is natural, whereas we'd like to know not what is natural but what happened and what the basis of the knowledge of the witness for that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question, Your Honour, was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm saying that the answer of the witness raises some concerns about his knowledge and therefore I would like you to be very specific, especially in this context, now, after having listened to the previous answers of the witness, what his source of knowledge is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pereula, in 1991, did you personally deal with the relocation of weapons that were intended for the war units of the TO in the work organisations?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at the next page of the B/C/S version and page 3 of the English version. Paragraph 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then we see here, it's the third paragraph from the bottom. It states: "Nonetheless, 64 municipal TO HQs which can deploy 452 war units and 120 TO headquarters." And then the last sentence says: "The storage problem has not been resolved fully." In 1991 did you deal with these municipal TO Staffs and the placement of the -- or the storage of the weapons?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would now like to show you the following page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And page 4 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that proposed measures are being referred to just now. And does this proposal of measures indicate that the process was not complete at the time this document was issued on the 13th of September, 1990?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that the process was not complete at the time. And that is precisely why I was included later. But I was not aware when these decisions were taken or the process of the decision-making. Once they were made, then I became a part of that process.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of item 1, it states: "The commander of the Territorial Defence of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina should adopt a special criterion to regulate the quantity of armaments and ammunition to be left with the TO HQ to protect the TO plants and facilities." Do you know whether the commander of the TO of the -- at that time Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was dealing with this issue after this?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: The order was that each staff had a war plan and a facility where there had to be a guard set up, so weapons were supposed to be left behind for that personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I hope that you are aware that the witness told us approximately an hour ago that he learned about all that only later and he had no knowledge about it. Everything happened after the multi-party elections. So you're now eliciting evidence from him on matters which he earlier said that he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He didn't know as of April as he was answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He said -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness said that this may all have happened, but he learned about matters only later. So apparently no direct --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- personal observation on the matter. I'm just pointing it to you so that we -- that you are aware of potential problems in interpreting the evidence, both for the parties and, of course, for the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I thought that introducing this witness to this document with only one paragraph that is contradicting the rest of the document has to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then, as I said before, we have to pay careful attention to the source of knowledge and the basis of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that my questions are only about the knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour. I would like -- I kindly ask to have page 5 in B/C/S and page 6 in English. In B/C/S, it's second paragraph; in English, it's the third paragraph on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pereula, were you aware at the time that there was a problem because it was not possible to have complete insight as to the security for the weapons for the DPO. Could you please tell us what the DPO is?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: DPO is the socio-political organisation, "Drustveno-Politicka Organizacija."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, the question was something different, but I was just concerned about the leading nature of going into that part of that. But I see the question was something different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, but the whole of the document is in evidence, so even if the witness wouldn't know anything about it, of course you can rely on the document itself. I mean, that's -- it's the Prosecution who tendered it. It's now evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you say they've not paid proper attention to other paragraphs, then of course you can rely on it if you wish to even if the witness doesn't know anything about it. The document is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I'm testing his knowledge about the events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I won't dwell for long and I won't raise any other issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pereula, did you know that weapons were obtained for the organs at the level of the republic and that they were relocated and placed in the Hadzici military weapons depot?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I -- I didn't hear the question very well. Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am waiting for the interpretation into English, so you need to wait a little bit.

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Oh, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time were you aware that the weapons obtained for the needs of the organs at the republican level were relocated to the military depot in Hadzici; and, if you are aware, could you please tell us when this was done?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your work, i.e., following the multi-party elections, was there still the problem that there were no proper conditions at the level of the republic to safely store these weapons?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, that was a problem, that the security was inadequate for the weapons of the TO. But all of this refers to 1991 which is what I am talking about. I don't know what was going on in 1990. This is the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I accept your explanation. We're just going to look at page 10 in the B/C/S and page 12 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before we do so, we were at the time where you would take a break, but if you say it's just a couple of minutes then we would most likely adjourn for the day and even for the week. I would be hesitant to restart for seven minutes or ten minutes after the break. But could you please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have two -- two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then two minutes, and Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I do have one document that I would just want to show quickly and seek its admission, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's a matter of minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: A matter of three questions but not necessarily -- it would be five minutes. Not more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then I suggest that we'll finish - but I'm also looking at Mr. Mladic - for another ten minutes so that we can adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pereula, let's look at paragraph 5, the second paragraph with a dash in both versions, which states: "Pending the resolution of all important defence and protection-related questions, it is proposed in the interim to store the armaments and ammunition of the socio-political organisations in TO or JNA depots." Are you aware that this was the temporary solution to store this materiel in the TO or JNA depots and that this was happening in 1990 and 1991 in the field, that ammunition and weaponry were being stored in the TO and the JNA depots?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, both in the TO depots which had adequate security, and where there were no proper conditions for this storage in the TO depots these weapons and ammunition were stored in JNA depots.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pereula, thank you very much. These were all our questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 18371.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up before you will be another document from SRBiH TO commander Bajcetic. It is an order he issued on the 23rd of October, 1990, regarding the gathering and submission of the remaining weaponry to the JNA warehouses. First of all could you read the order and let us know if that is the same or a different order than you are referring to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: That is not that order. I'm referring to the order by the town commander Vukosavljevic, he was the town commander, and before he met with General Bajcetic. What I said refers to a different order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I just wanted to show you this quickly and I understand you claimed a lack of knowledge about a lot of things. But since Mr. Lukic raised the issue that was there was remaining steps to be taken, I put it to you that the republican TO did, in fact, shortly after that September report, take further steps. Is it your evidence that you were not aware of this?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: These further steps as described on the 23rd of October 1990 which included, according to part 1, ammunition and MES from the social and public companies, which I believe was just discussed with you with Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: SPIRO PEREULA
utterances.text: The order was not completely executed until 1991. It was only in 1991 after General Vukosavljevic became the commander and then he issued a separate order to complete the process, and also it was idea that nobody could issue weapons or ammunition from any of the depots without his explicit order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. You really haven't answered my question but I'm not going to labour on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender 65 ter 18371 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6917, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. No further questions, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And thank you for the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Pereula, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, a very long way, and for having answered the questions, questions put to you by the party, questions put to you by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When the witness end the courtroom, I briefly raised the matter of 1D1 -- 1D01730, 40 pages. Any position? Mr. Traldi, it seems you're the one who is involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for clarity of the record, I think it's 1D02733 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- that I'm being asked about. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are right. You are right. And I must admit that there is a typo somewhere because in my papers it's -- it gives two times the right one. But there was a problem about it anyhow, isn't it, so -- but we are talking about 1D02733.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm relieved to that hear that, Mr. President, as I was not prepared to address the other document. As -- the Prosecution maintains its position, as I think I briefly stated Tuesday, that we don't object to the admission of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby on the record. We'll decide on the matter. No, there's no objection. I think we can admit it. No number has yet been assigned, I think. Mr. Registrar, for 1D02733 what number would be assigned?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D781, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D781 is admitted into evidence. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have one left over, that is the video, the associated exhibits. Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for Mr. Registrar. I forgot about it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, he was -- the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Having read the transcript meanwhile, the Chamber does not insist on viewing. Any -- there were no objections, Mr. Weber, although there is an understanding that whatever the reporters say is not -- the Defence will not rely on that and purely on - and I've forgotten of the person - but who tell us what happened in this cellar of this cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Brica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Brica. Under those circumstances and with this understanding, Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D782, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D782 is admitted into evidence. Are there any other matters? If not, we'll adjourn and we'll resume Monday, the 16th -- let me just -- no, the 17th of November. That's Monday morning, 9.30, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
